name: Arm warmers (alt style)

card.summary: Knitted sleeves worn over the forearms that add layered texture to scene, emo, goth, e-girl and femboy outfits.

quick.overview:
Arm warmers are knitted sleeves that cover the lower arm, often without finger coverings. In alt fashion they are worn for the look: striped or solid sleeves add contrast and layering to an outfit.

Punk, emo, scene and goth subcultures adopted them as a fashion statement, and they are also used by dancers and endurance athletes for warmth.
quick.how: They are slipped over the forearm and worn with short-sleeved tops, often in pairs of contrasting stripes or dark colours. The effect is immediate and removable.
quick.risks: No safety concerns specific to the style; compression sports versions are used for warmth and sun protection.

lead: Arm warmers are knitted sleeves for the arms; the term can also cover glove-like items without finger coverings that were originally meant to keep wrists and lower arms warm.[1] Dancers wear them to warm up before class, and they became a seasonal fashion item.[1]

Punk, emo, scene and goth subcultures adopted them as a fashion statement.[1] In current alt styling they are a common accessory for scene, e-girl and femboy looks, where they add layering and contrast to a short-sleeved top. The effect lasts only while worn.

Endurance athletes wear Lycra sleeves for insulation and UV protection.[1] One small study of twelve men examined the effect of arm insulation on physiological responses during running in the cold.[2]

chain: Adds layered, patterned detail to an outfit
angle.text: Arm warmers change how an outfit reads by adding stripes, colour or texture at the forearm. They are used to signal an alt aesthetic.

paras: Arm warmers are tube-like sleeves worn on the forearm.[1] Sports versions in spandex or Lycra are said to reduce arm muscle swelling and lactic acid build-up, insulate in cold and provide UV protection.[1]
Punk, emo, scene and goth subcultures adopted arm warmers as a fashion statement.[1] During the 2010 FIFA World Cup, team-themed arm warmers became a phenomenon in South Africa and abroad.[1]
A 2018 study of twelve healthy men found in a cold environment during running that arm insulation was examined for its effect on physiological responses; this concerns warmth, not appearance.[2]

refs.title: Effects of arm insulation on physiological responses during running in the cold.
